text:
alex: shelf-22 showing repeated NVMe write storms, 99p gen latency spikes ~2s, started 01:06 UTC. Some dedicated slices impacted. Leaving here for quick ops sync.
maria: saw it. top hosts show tx_burst + kvcache regen. likely dataset upload churn from a single tenant. can we apply a soft egress cap while we ID culprit?
jin: propose immediate action: router-side soft cap 50Mbps for slice-dedicated-67 and enable 3min spillback window. command:
```
curl -X POST http://router-api/v1/routing/shape -d '{"slice":"slice-dedicated-67","bandwidth_mbps":50,"spillback_secs":180}'
```
apply canary 10% first.
carmen: agree on canary. also request infra-bot to list top 6 write tenants on shelf-22 last 10m. if tenant repeats after shaping, plan ephemeral move to fractional-carveout for 30m and replay.
infra-bot: top_writers: ["tenant-221","tenant-824","tenant-1301","tenant-402"] avg_iops: [6100,4200,1800,700] (01:00-01:10 UTC).
alex: thanks. jin, roll 10% fallback and tag metric=egress-shape-1744449876. Carmen, please draft the quarantine rule: auto-quarantine if tenant causes >2 NVMe spikes in 12h. cost note: ephemeral carveout ~+$450/hr.
maria: shaping applied to slice-dedicated-67 canary 10%. infra-bot shows 99p down to 260ms in 90s.
infra-bot: shaping applied by maria. monitoring 10m window.
jin: if stable, increase to 40% then full. recommend a follow-up: add shelf_io_depth SLI and a dashboard per slice for kvcache regen.
carmen: created TICKET-1029 to formalize quarantine rule and ask finance for carveout budget.
alex: good work. keep logs in TICKET-1029 and upload host iostat + router logs. escalate if warm-reserve latency >700ms. :thumbsup:
